Installation

This page describes the software needed to run the CPU PROMISE benchmark suite and the optional H100 CUDA validation scripts.

Prerequisites

For CPU precision-search experiments:

  • Python 3.9 or newer.

  • g++ with C++11 support.

  • CADNA, activated through the bundled cadnaPromise package or through a local CADNA installation.

  • Python packages used by the run and plotting scripts: numpy, matplotlib, colorama, colorlog, tqdm, regex, pyyaml, packaging, and docopt-ng or docopt.

  • GNU Parallel is optional but recommended for run_benchmarks.sh --parallel.

For H100 validation experiments:

  • NVIDIA CUDA with nvcc.

  • An H100-capable CUDA architecture target, normally sm_90.

  • On Jean Zay, an H100 allocation such as ${IDRPROJ}@h100.

Clone The Repository

git clone https://github.com/PEQUAN/hpc-mix-bench.git
cd hpc-mix-bench

Install CADNA/PROMISE

The repository bundles the cadnaPromise Python package. A local editable install is convenient when running from a cluster account:

cd cadnaPromise
python3 -m pip install --user -e .
export PATH="$(python3 -m site --user-base)/bin:$PATH"
activate-promise

Verify that the command-line tools are visible:

which promise
which activate-promise
python3 -c "import cadnaPromise; print(cadnaPromise.__file__)"

Install Python Dependencies

On systems with internet access:

python3 -m pip install --user numpy matplotlib colorama colorlog tqdm regex pyyaml packaging docopt-ng

On clusters where compute nodes do not have network access, install these packages on a login node before submitting jobs. The batch scripts add the user base bin directory to PATH and the user site-packages directory to PYTHONPATH when needed.

Docker

Docker provides a reproducible CPU environment for PROMISE and plotting.

On Linux x86_64 and Windows on Intel/AMD:

docker build -t hpc-mix-cadna .
docker run -it --rm hpc-mix-cadna

On macOS Apple Silicon and Windows on ARM:

docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t hpc-mix-cadna .
docker run --platform linux/amd64 -it --rm hpc-mix-cadna

The repository also provides a Docker Compose service:

docker compose run --rm promise-env

ReadTheDocs

The online documentation is built with Sphinx. To reproduce the build locally:

python3 -m pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
python3 -m sphinx -b html docs/source docs/_build/html

ReadTheDocs uses the repository-level .readthedocs.yaml file and installs docs/requirements.txt before building docs/source.
